marks.anchor: The work has two focused contributions
marks.added: The work has two focused contributions. First, it introduces a decision-time validation layer that turns an energy study request into a checked specification of the reserve task, data boundary, cost setting, and required evidence. Second, it connects that specification to reproducible reserve-calibration comparisons and traces changes in the study fields to their numerical consequences. Interface comparisons evaluate interpretation, admissibility, completion, and preparation workload. Public-data policy comparisons evaluate reserve cost, empirical coverage, and tail shortfall under common reliability requirements; a separate controlled residual-state diagnostic examines calibration sensitivity in the archived regional study.

marks.anchor: In the public quarter-hourly comparison
marks.added: In the public quarter-hourly comparison, 700 days fit the base upper-quantile model, followed by 20 days for calibration fitting, ten days for selection, and 30 days for testing. Residuals are realized ramps minus their base predictions. Global calibration uses one upper residual quantile; local calibration uses residuals from observations with a similar decision-time state. The public selected-local policy uses a fixed load, ramp, calendar, and predicted-quantile state and selects its shrinkage value on the ten-day selection block. Its calibration residuals remain those from the earlier 20 days. The archived regional adaptive procedure also selects a residual-state representation and subsequently refits its chosen calibrator on the full 30-day calibration block.

marks.anchor: Within each numerical protocol
marks.added: Within each numerical protocol, reserve policies share the target, decision-time information boundary, evaluation windows, and cost function. The comparison includes different prediction and calibration rules. In the eight-policy public comparison, seven policies share the base quantile prediction, while the static policy estimates a target quantile directly from the calibration-fit observations. All eight use the same calibration-fit and selection periods and empirical selection requirement. The request-validation procedure is evaluated first as a request-processing procedure. Accepted study fields then specify the numerical calculation and remain linked to its outputs.

marks.anchor: For the public-data selection screen
marks.added: For the public-data selection screen, let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the evaluated policy configurations.

marks.anchor: The archived regional comparison set contains
marks.added: The archived regional comparison set contains a static reserve rule, a linear quantile-regression policy, and weather-informed and weather-agnostic histogram-gradient-boosting quantile models.

marks.anchor: The public-data comparison evaluates eight policies
marks.added: The public-data comparison evaluates eight policies: a static target quantile, the base quantile predictor, global calibration, local calibration, selected-local shrinkage, horizon-block maximum calibration, scenario quantiles, and scenario maxima. Its selected-local policy chooses a direct mixture of local and global residual quantiles. Scenario pools use four states defined by whether current load and recent observed ramps exceed their training-period 80th percentiles. The Supplementary Material specifies the candidate mixtures, neighborhood weighting, and common selection offset.

marks.anchor: The archived regional study defines four diagnostic regimes
marks.added: The archived regional study defines four diagnostic regimes from each model-fitting sample: \textit{high load}, \textit{hot and humid}, \textit{compound heat-stress}, and \textit{volatile}. The threshold for each component is the 80th percentile of the corresponding model-fitting distribution. The compound heat-stress regime requires high temperature, high humidity, and high load simultaneously. These regimes locate concentrations of coverage errors and cost reductions and provide the historical stochastic and robust residual scenario pools. The public-data diagnostics instead report seasonal groups and high-ramp periods defined from recent observed ramps, alongside the four load--ramp states used for its scenario policies.

marks.anchor: The main reserve evaluation uses public quarter-hourly national load
marks.added: The main reserve evaluation uses public quarter-hourly national load for Germany, Austria, Belgium, and the Netherlands from the Open Power System Data (OPSD) time-series package. Twelve 30-day test windows per country beginning in January 2019 provide 138,240 held-out decisions. A frozen-margin extension evaluates eight later windows per country beginning in January 2020, providing 92,160 further decisions. Load, reserve, and shortfall are expressed in megawatts (MW). Section~\ref{subsec:overall_results} reports both comparisons.

marks.anchor: The public evaluation uses chronological
marks.added: The public evaluation uses chronological 700-day fitting, 20-day residual-calibration, ten-day selection, and 30-day test blocks. Target end times precede the next block's first decision time. Calibration residuals determine global and local corrections, block maxima, and scenario pools; the selection block determines shrinkage and the offset required for 0.95 selection coverage. The fitted model, residual pool, and selected settings remain fixed during testing. Twelve 2019 test windows per country provide the initial benchmark.

marks.anchor: For the later-window comparison, each country receives
marks.added: For the later-window comparison, each country receives a margin estimated from the 2019 benchmark. For each benchmark policy and window, we compute the 95th percentile of realized target-minus-reserve differences, truncate it at zero, and divide by that window's calibration-fit mean load. The largest fraction across the eight policies and twelve benchmark windows is then held fixed across eight test windows beginning in January 2020. Cost intervals use 3,000 circular moving-block draws with three consecutive windows per block and Bonferroni adjustment across four countries. Separate checks vary the block length.

marks.anchor: The archived anonymized study uses
marks.added: The archived anonymized study uses 700 fitting days, 30 calibration days, 30 test days, and a 30-day rolling step, yielding 86 test windows. Its adaptive residual-state procedure divides calibration into 20 fitting days and ten selection days, then refits the selected calibrator on all 30 days. Its original uncertainty summaries use 20,000 resamples of the 86 windows with replacement.

marks.anchor: Figure~\ref{fig:state_density} relates
marks.added: Figure~\ref{fig:state_density} relates two observed calibration-state components to the realized reserve target in the public benchmark. Each country contributes 34,560 held-out decisions from twelve 2019 windows. The horizontal axis gives current load, the vertical axis gives the largest observed positive ramp over the twelve most recent quarter-hour observations, and color gives the mean subsequent one-hour target within each populated hexagon. Load and recent ramps are available at the decision time; the subsequent target enters the descriptive summary after realization.

marks.anchor: Target magnitudes vary across load--ramp states
marks.added: Target magnitudes vary across load--ramp states and countries. The public local calibrator combines load and ramp statistics with calendar coordinates and the base quantile prediction. The policy comparison evaluates the cost and reliability of the resulting residual corrections. Weather-based residual-state diagnostics from the original regional study are retained in the Supplementary Material.

marks.anchor: For request $i$, let $E_i$
marks.added: For request $i$, let $E_i$ be the mean expert preparation estimate in seconds and $A_{ij}$ the measured return latency for service trial $j$. The derived review-time budget is $B_{ij}=E_i-A_{ij}$. A preparation workflow with review time $V_{ij}$ has total time $A_{ij}+V_{ij}$ and falls below $E_i$ when $V_{ij}<B_{ij}$. Median paired budgets are 175.4, 170.3, 160.6, and 155.6 seconds for DeepSeek, Qwen, ERNIE, and Hunyuan.

marks.anchor: The complete time analysis adds review
marks.added: The complete time analysis adds review, correction, and the remaining preparation tasks to measured service time. For trial $j$ of request $i$, let $m_{ij}$ count reviewed entries and $r_{ij}$ count minimum replacements. With review time $v$ per entry, correction time $c$ per replacement, and other preparation time $o$, the conditional total is $T_{ij}=A_{ij}+vm_{ij}+cr_{ij}+o$. The grid uses five review values from 10 to 60 seconds, three correction values from 5 to 30 seconds, and three other-task values from 0 to 60 seconds, giving 180 service-specific conditions.

marks.added: Figure~\ref{fig:r1_service_interfaces} separates historical joint success from independently labelled disposition accuracy. The paired interface--parser differences change after validation; all ten Holm-adjusted parser comparisons exceed 0.05 at each endpoint.

marks.anchor: For each country, we estimated a nonnegative reliability margin
marks.added: For each country, we estimated a nonnegative reliability margin from the 2019 benchmark windows as a fraction of calibration-fit mean load. This fraction is common to all eight policies and is held fixed for eight later windows beginning in 2020. All 256 policy-window combinations reached at least 0.95 empirical coverage; the lowest window coverage was 0.952.

marks.anchor: Under the frozen-margin protocol, selected-local mean cost gains
marks.added: Under the frozen-margin protocol, selected-local mean cost gains over global calibration are 0.000026, 0.000187, 0.000068, and 0.000163 in Germany, Austria, Belgium, and the Netherlands. These are reductions of 0.13, 0.68, 0.20, and 0.81 percent relative to global cost, respectively. Table~\ref{tab:r1_frozen_intervals} reports paired intervals from 3,000 circular moving-block draws, using three consecutive monthly windows and Bonferroni adjustment for the four-country comparison. Only the Austria and Netherlands intervals have positive lower endpoints.

marks.anchor: An auxiliary weather diagnostic uses
marks.added: An auxiliary weather diagnostic uses equal-weight temperature and relative humidity from six official German Weather Service stations, with a one-hour availability lag. Across eight 30-day windows and 23,040 decisions per variant, adding weather reduces base-predictor pinball loss from 31.10 to 30.56 MW and selected-local cost index from 0.01968 to 0.01953. Both input variants have coverage below 0.95 in several test windows; their minimum window coverages are 0.922 for calendar-only inputs and 0.919 with weather.

marks.anchor: Table~\ref{tab:r1_physical} expresses reserve
marks.added: Table~\ref{tab:r1_physical} expresses reserve and shortfall in MW for the 2019 benchmark. The tail measure averages the largest five percent of shortfalls, with fractional weighting at the quantile boundary. The cost index uses reserve holding weight one and shortfall weight twenty.

marks.anchor: The block comparison uses the maximum calibration residual
marks.added: The block comparison uses the maximum calibration residual within complete, nonoverlapping horizon-length groups. It provides a dependence-aware empirical calibration reference.

marks.anchor: The Supplementary Material reports these correlations
marks.added: The Supplementary Material reports these correlations, effective neighborhood size, seasonal and high-ramp prediction loss and calibrated reliability, and sensitivities to calibration length, neighborhood size, effective sample size, and reliability threshold. High-ramp states use a threshold estimated from the training period.

marks.anchor: The calculation replay transfers region, horizon, and shortfall weight
marks.added: The calculation replay transfers region, horizon, and shortfall weight directly from service responses for 22 independently authored requests with public United States load data. Five responses per service produce 110 paired trials. This protocol uses 180 days for fitting, 20 for residual calibration, ten for selection, and 30 for testing.

marks.anchor: Nine checked public-data study plans vary
marks.added: Nine checked public-data study plans vary region, horizon, admissible variables, shortfall weight, reliability requirement, and reporting requirements.

marks.anchor: A change in region changes the load series
marks.added: A change in region changes the load series and calibration distribution. A change from 60 to 120 or 180 minutes changes the future target construction. Restricting the variables to load history and calendar changes the fitted predictor. Changing the shortfall weight changes the quantile objective.

marks.anchor: Changing the reliability requirement changes
marks.added: Changing the reliability requirement changes the common selection offset. Adding tail-shortfall reporting changes the returned evidence while retaining the same reserve series.

marks.anchor: Under a common German reference target
marks.added: Under a common German reference target with 2,880 decision timestamps, changing the region to Austria lowers reference-target coverage to 0.430 and raises the normalized cost difference to +0.10153. Extending the horizon to 120 and 180 minutes raises mean reserve by 207.3 and 460.2 MW and raises the cost difference by +0.00293 and +0.00660.

marks.anchor: Reducing the predictor variables
marks.added: Reducing the predictor variables to load history and calendar changes mean reserve by 13.7 MW and cost by +0.00028. Increasing the shortfall weight to 40 changes cost by +0.00118, while weight 10 changes it by -0.00002. Raising the required coverage to 0.975 changes mean reserve by 84.0 MW and cost by +0.00073.

marks.anchor: Across the four-service replay's 440 trials, 266 pass validation
marks.added: Across the four-service replay's 440 trials, 266 pass validation and enter the offline numerical replay, 174 return for further preparation, and 362 produce a numerically interpretable candidate plan. Interpretable candidates supply the field comparison; the fixed checks determine execution eligibility.

marks.anchor: Completed validated plans reproduce the reference reserve series and have zero paired cost difference
marks.added: Completed validated plans reproduce the reference reserve series and have zero paired cost difference. The supplementary outcome table reports measured service time, token budget, and field corrections for executed and returned plans.

marks.anchor: The six-field extension connects actual service responses
marks.added: The six-field extension connects actual service responses to all six categories of study specification through offline calculation replay. Its nine complete requests produce 180 initial trials, of which 149 pass field validation and select their recorded numerical calculation. Complete-request executions number 45, 45, 17, and 42 out of 45 for DeepSeek, Qwen, ERNIE, and Hunyuan. The three omission requests produce sixty initial trials and sixty confirmation responses; 47 confirmed plans reach calculation, with service counts of 11, 10, 11, and 15 out of 15.

marks.anchor: Each of the nine complete specifications produces
marks.added: Each of the nine complete specifications produces at least thirteen actual executions across the services. The executed records preserve source-response hashes, target and reserve hashes, and the requested numerical report. Tail reporting adds the tail-shortfall result while retaining the same reserve series.

marks.anchor: We also inject one field deviation
marks.added: We also inject one field deviation into an actual accepted response while keeping its request fixed. Six categories produce 95 controlled deviations, and validation returns all 95 for confirmation. The region deviation would give 0.430 reference-target coverage and a +0.101534 cost difference; the horizon, variable, weight, and reliability deviations would give +0.002925, +0.000285, +0.001176, and +0.000734. Removing requested tail reporting changes the report contents while preserving reserve and cost.

marks.added: Among all eight policies, the lowest mean cost is achieved by the quantile predictor in Germany, the scenario quantile in Austria and Belgium, and selected-local calibration in the Netherlands. In the Netherlands, selected-local cost is 0.26 percent below the next-lowest cost, obtained by ordinary local calibration.

marks.added: Figure~\ref{fig:r1_conditional_bandwidth} places the 2019 conditional coverage beside the German bandwidth results. marks.anchor: The time profile in Figure~\ref{fig:r1_public_trajectory} uses
marks.added: The time profile in Figure~\ref{fig:r1_public_trajectory} uses the first seven days of the fourth later German window. The reserve trajectories include the frozen common margin. State-dependent calibration raises and lowers reserve relative to global correction at different decision times, while the quantile predictor supplies the lowest-cost German reference in the eight-policy comparison.

marks.anchor: Figure~\ref{fig:r1_field_consequences} connects
marks.added: Figure~\ref{fig:r1_field_consequences} connects the controlled specification changes to their numerical consequences and shows completion in the separate independent-request replay. A reporting-only change preserves reserve and cost. Region and horizon changes alter the calculated decision, while the service completion counts identify how many validated plans reach their request-specific offline calculation.

marks.added: Every interface then requires the same check of decision-time information, supported parameters, evidence, and authorization. On the 48 independently authored requests, the tested language-service configurations have zero unsafe execution-ready plans, while the parser retains four after the same validation checks. Expert-entered forms also have zero unsafe readiness in the 24-request comparison. These outcomes reflect the combination of request interpretation and subsequent validation.

marks.added: The experiment on complete drafts evaluates how much supplied content reaches review under a separate field-preserving protocol.
